sets.title: Fixed-point scale, rounding and saturation

objective_text.T64.01.a: Derive and defend: Derive the product scale and prove int32_t multiplication and negation bounds before implementing absolute value. Separate saturation policy from the rounding rule.
objective_text.T64.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement ns_q15(a,b) for signed Q1.15 operands: multiply exactly in int32_t, round the scaled result to nearest with ties away from zero, then saturate into [-32768,32767]. In particular -32768 times -32768 saturates to32767. Derive the range of every intermediate and distinguish quantization error from saturation.
objective_text.T64.01.c: Falsify and transfer: The mutant truncates toward zero, failing positive and negative half-way cases. A signed right shift is not a portable replacement for the specified rounding rule. Then Change to Q3.12 and compare wrap, saturate and error-return APIs. Derive a dot-product accumulator width from maximum length instead of copying the Q1.15 constants.

sets.title: Exact rounding model and ties to even

objective_text.T64.02.a: Derive and defend: Derive nearest-neighbor intervals and parity at exact ties. Prove remainder doubling is avoided by comparing r with denominator-r, and explain the negative sign symmetry.
objective_text.T64.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement ns_round_even(numerator,denominator,out) for numerator in[-1000000,1000000] and denominator in[1,1000000]. Return the nearest integer, breaking exact ties toward an even integer; leave out unchanged on invalid input. Use integer quotient/remainder, with no floating conversion or rounding library.

Distinguish conversion behavior from arithmetic rounding.

sets.title: Accuracy admission and exceptional values

objective_text.T64.08.a: Derive and defend: Derive the asymmetric expected-relative policy, near-zero behavior and exceptional-value handling. Explain rounding at the acceptance boundary and why a tolerance must come from a prior requirement or error analysis.
objective_text.T64.08.b: Implement and investigate: Implement ns_close(actual,expected,atol,rtol) for finite values and finite tolerances with0<=atol and0<=rtol<=1. Use the mathematical target |actual-expected|<=atol+rtol*|expected| and define actual admission by the supplied rounded scaled comparison (boundary rounding is part of this contract), scaling to avoid overflow in difference or threshold. NaN and infinities are rejected, including equal infinities. This is an admission predicate, not proof of an algorithm error bound.
objective_text.T64.08.c: Falsify and transfer: The mutant removes the absolute component, rejecting a permitted near-zero error. Conversely a loose tolerance selected after seeing failures can hide a wrong algorithm. Then Construct condition-sensitive and metamorphic tests whose predictions do not use the implementation output as the oracle. Compare ulp-based and absolute/relative policies around subnormals, signed zero and an ill-conditioned problem.
